question: How far can the bus be leaned sideways on a tilt rig before it is allowed to roll over?
answer: It must not reach the overturning point when the platform is tilted to 28° from horizontal, to each side in turn.

question: What are the minimum height and width of an emergency door opening on a full-size bus of Class I, II or III?
answer: At least 1,450 mm high and 600 mm wide.

question: If a power-operated door closes on someone, how much squeezing force is tolerated before it has to reopen?
answer: The door must reopen fully when resisted by a clamping force of no more than 150 N; a brief peak above 150 N is allowed as long as it stays under 300 N.

question: Какая минимальная освещённость нужна на полу прохода, когда работает аварийное освещение салона?
answer: Не менее 1 люкса на уровне пола по осевой линии проходов и проходов к дверям, а также в центре каждой ступени.
notes: Related: 10 lux at 750 mm height is in 7.8.3.7 but the question asks about floor level.

question: What is the minimum seat pitch between rows of forward-facing seats in an intercity coach (Class II or III)?
answer: 680 mm, measured horizontally from the front of one seat back to the back of the seat in front (650 mm for Classes I, A and B).
notes: The regulation calls this 'seat spacing' (dimension H).

question: How big does the dedicated area for one wheelchair user inside the bus have to be?
answer: At least 750 mm wide, 1,300 mm long and 1,400 mm high, aligned with the vehicle's longitudinal axis.

question: What minimum platform size and rated load does a wheelchair lift need?
answer: The platform must be at least 800 mm wide and 1,200 mm long and work with a load of at least 300 kg.

question: How steep may a wheelchair ramp be when deployed to a 150 mm kerb, and when deployed straight to the road?
answer: Not more than 12 % onto a 150 mm kerb and not more than 36 % to the ground; kneeling may be used to achieve this.

question: At what earth leakage level does a trolleybus have to isolate itself from the overhead wires on its own?
answer: When the leakage current between chassis and road exceeds 3 mA or the leakage voltage exceeds 60 V DC (disconnection applies when the trolleybus is stationary).

question: During the re-ignition test of an engine-bay fire extinguishing system, how long must the fire stay out?
answer: No re-ignition is allowed for 45 seconds after the fire has been completely put out.
notes: Same 45 s requirement appears for component approval (Part 1) and for a specific engine compartment (Part 2); both listed.

question: What is the maximum height of the first step above the road at the service door of a Class III coach?
answer: 380 mm for at least one service door (400 mm for other service doors; 430 mm if the vehicle has purely mechanical suspension).
notes: Answer is in the Figure 8 table and footnotes (Annex 4, p. 84, read from PDF). If the coach is fitted for reduced-mobility access, Annex 8 3.1 imposes 320 mm for at least one door; question is about the general limit.

question: When the bus is fully loaded, what share of its maximum mass has to rest on the driven axle(s)?
answer: At least 25 % of the technically permissible maximum laden mass M.

question: What qualifies a bus as 'low floor' under UN R107?
answer: A Class I, II or A vehicle where at least 35 % of the standing area (front section for articulated, lower deck for double-deckers) is step-free and includes access to at least one service door.

question: Что означает «Класс II» для автобусов по Правилам ООН № 107?
answer: Автобус вместимостью более 22 пассажиров, предназначенный в основном для сидящих пассажиров; стоящие допускаются только в проходе и/или на площади не больше, чем занимают два двойных сиденья.

question: What does the regulation mean by the superstructure of a bus body?
answer: The load-bearing part of the bodywork that gives the vehicle its strength if it rolls over.

question: Which voltage range puts a trolleybus circuit into Class B?
answer: Rated voltage above 30 V up to 1,000 V AC, and above 60 V up to 1,500 V DC.
notes: The ≤ signs are dropped in blocks.jsonl text; confirmed from the rendered PDF page 129.

question: For trolleybus electrics, how is basic insulation different from supplementary insulation?
answer: Basic insulation protects people from electrical hazards in systems that have protective bonding; supplementary insulation does so in systems without protective bonding. Together they form double insulation.

question: Кого Правила относят к пассажирам с ограниченной мобильностью?
answer: Всех, кому трудно пользоваться общественным транспортом: инвалидов (включая колясочников, людей с сенсорными и интеллектуальными нарушениями, нарушениями конечностей), людей маленького роста, пожилых, беременных, пассажиров с тяжёлым багажом, тележками для покупок или с детьми, в том числе в колясках.

question: Does R107 cover buses built specifically to take children to school?
answer: No. Vehicles specially designed for carrying school children are excluded from the regulation's requirements.

question: We are building a mobile library on a bus chassis. Do we have to meet all of R107?
answer: Only as far as the requirements are compatible with its use, provided it carries no more than 8 people (excluding the driver) while moving; the seats used while driving must be clearly identified.

question: Is an automatic extinguishing system in the engine bay mandatory for a small Class A or B minibus with a rear engine?
answer: No. Classes I, II and III must have one; Classes A and B only need the over-temperature alarm and may optionally fit a fire suppression system.
notes: Applies to vehicles with a combustion engine or combustion heater behind the driver's compartment.

question: Обязана ли быть система аварийного освещения в городском автобусе класса I?
answer: Нет. Обязательна она только для классов II, III и B; для класса I не требуется (если установлена — должна включаться при пожарной тревоге).
notes: Parenthetical refers to 7.5.7.1(a) ('if fitted'); the core answer is 7.8.3.

question: Can a trolleybus have emergency escape hatches in its roof?
answer: No. Roof escape hatches are prohibited on trolleybuses.
notes: 7.6.1.12 (no hatches near high-voltage systems) is related but the explicit trolleybus ban is in 7.6.1.11.

question: Do intercity and long-distance coaches have to be wheelchair accessible, or is that only for city buses?
answer: Only Class I must be accessible (at least one wheelchair user and one pram/pushchair). For other classes it is up to the Contracting Parties, but any accessibility features that are fitted must comply with Annex 8.

question: Does the driver's seat in a Class B minibus need a suspension and height adjustment?
answer: No. Suspension and vertical adjustment are required in general but are not mandatory for Classes A and B; fore-aft and backrest adjustment with automatic locking still apply.
notes: Exemption is in 7.7.14.7.1 (subsection of the gold).

question: How steep can the aisle be in a city bus compared with a touring coach, and is the wheelchair route held to a tighter limit?
answer: Lengthwise: 8 % for Classes I, II, A and 12.5 % for Classes III and B; crosswise 5 % for all. The path from a wheelchair space to an entrance/exit is limited to 5 % (8 % from priority seats).

question: How do the static test loads on wheelchair tie-down anchorages differ between M2 and M3 buses?
answer: M2: 1,110 ± 20 daN forward and 550 ± 20 daN rearward. M3: 740 ± 20 daN forward and 370 ± 20 daN rearward. In both cases applied 200–300 mm above the wheelchair space floor.
notes: Hybrid-test anchorages (3.8.3); the static-test route in 3.8.2 has different values.

question: Насколько меньше может быть аварийная дверь у микроавтобуса класса A или B по сравнению с большим автобусом?
answer: Для классов I–III проём не менее 1 450 × 600 мм; для классов A и B по альтернативным требованиям — 1 250 × 550 мм, а ширина может уменьшаться до 300 мм у колёсных арок при сохранении 550 мм на высоте от 400 мм.
notes: Annex 7 table is in blocks with section null under heading 1.1 (p. 105).

question: If the first attempt of a fire extinguishing test fails, what retest rule applies for a component-approved system versus one approved for a specific engine bay?
answer: Component approval: pass if two of three attempts succeed. Specific engine compartment: both the second and the third attempts must succeed.
notes: Same rule repeated for low-load, fan and re-ignition tests (Part 1 1.4.3/1.5.3/1.6.3; Part 2 1.5.3/1.6.3/1.7.3). Gold uses the high-load test sections; reviewer may want to add the others. Wording difference is subtle.

question: What distinguishes a Class A minibus from a Class B one?
answer: Both carry up to 22 passengers. Class A has seats plus provision for standing passengers; Class B has no provision for standees.

question: For the tilt test of a city bus, how much ballast goes on each passenger seat?
answer: A mass Q per seat; for Class I (and A) Q is 68 kg (71 kg for Classes II, III and B, including 3 kg of hand baggage).
notes: The Q table is printed on p. 125 directly after 3.2.3.2.1; in blocks.jsonl the table rows have section_number null. If chunks attribute it differently, gold may need page 125.

question: Where on a power-operated door should the anti-pinch force be measured?
answer: At the main closing edges: one point in the middle of the door and one 150 mm above its lower edge (plus the most dangerous point of secondary edges if anti-clamping for opening is fitted); the limit checked is 150 N.

question: Какой контраст должны иметь кнопки связи с водителем у приоритетных мест и по какой формуле он считается?
answer: Контраст C ≥ 0,4 и диффузное отражение не менее 0,5 (либо кнопка белая или жёлтая). C = |ρ1 − ρ2| / (ρ1 + ρ2), где ρ1 — отражение материала объекта, ρ2 — окружающей поверхности.
notes: Formula symbols (ρ) are dropped in blocks.jsonl; formula confirmed from the rendered PDF page 101.

question: What symbol must be displayed on the outside of a bus with a wheelchair space, and how large must it be?
answer: The wheelchair-user pictogram (Figure 23A): white symbol on blue, at least 130 mm in diameter, shown on the front nearside and next to the relevant service door(s), plus one inside at each wheelchair space.

question: Our extinguishing system was type-approved as a component. How do we size it for a rear engine bay with 6 m³ gross volume?
answer: The component's documented agent mass and discharge points refer to a 4 m³ compartment. Above 4 m³ scale up with Sx = 0.1·x + 0.6, i.e. 1.2 for 6 m³: about 20 % more agent, discharge points and propellant, at the same system pressure. Gross volume is used (engine volume not subtracted).
notes: Annex 1 item; 4 m³ reference also in 2.4/2.5 of that appendix.

question: Сколько приоритетных мест нужно в автобусе класса I и на какой высоте должен идти поручень от них до двери?
answer: Не менее четырёх приоритетных мест; поручень на высоте 800–900 мм от пола между ними и хотя бы одной служебной дверью, разрывы не более 1 050 мм с вертикальным поручнем хотя бы с одной стороны разрыва.

question: What turning circle does a bus need to be able to fit inside?
answer: It must complete a full 360° circle on either side within a ring between an outer radius of 12.5 m and an inner radius of 5.3 m.
notes: Document says 'manoeuvrability' and 'concentric circles', never 'turning circle'.

question: Can we put movie screens for passengers where the driver can see them?
answer: No. Passenger entertainment displays must be outside the driver's view from the normal driving position; screens used by the driver for operating the vehicle (e.g. door monitoring) are allowed.

question: How high can the stop-request buttons be mounted in a city bus?
answer: No higher than 1,500 mm above the floor (extra higher ones may be added); they must be operable with the palm and spread evenly through the vehicle.
notes: Document says 'communication devices' / 'signal that the driver should stop'.

question: Does every glass break-out window need an emergency hammer next to it?
answer: Yes, for emergency windows of readily-breakable safety glass a breaking device must be provided next to each one; for rear windows it goes centrally above or below, or one at each end.
notes: Document never says 'hammer'.

question: Можно ли ехать, если автобус ещё «присевший» на остановке?
answer: Только медленно: пока кузов опущен ниже нормальной дорожной высоты, система не должна позволять двигаться быстрее 5 км/ч.
notes: Colloquial 'присевший' for kneeling system.

question: How much clearance is needed between combustible trim and hot parts like the tailpipe or turbo?
answer: No flammable material within 100 mm of exhaust components, high-voltage equipment or other significant heat sources unless it is effectively shielded.
notes: Requirement text is an unnumbered block directly under heading 7.5.5 (p. 47).

question: What is the maximum overall length allowed for an articulated city bus?
notes: Annex 11 only defines how length is measured (ISO 612) and requires the turning-circle test; no length limit. Searched 'maximum length', '18.75', '12.0 m': no hits except service-door lighting zone.

question: What is the test procedure for checking the strength of the bus body in a rollover?
notes: Only the definition of superstructure (Reg 2.4) mentions roll-over; no test. Searched 'roll-over', 'rollover', 'Regulation No. 66'. Retrieval may surface 2.4 — it does not answer.

question: What is the maximum allowed interior noise level at the driver's seat?
notes: Searched 'noise', 'dB': no hits.

question: Are there thermal runaway requirements for the traction battery of a battery-electric bus?
notes: Searched 'REESS', 'thermal runaway', 'traction batter', 'rechargeable': none. Annex 3 7.5.3 has generic battery mounting/ventilation rules and Annex 12 3.6 battery case materials for trolleybuses, neither addresses thermal runaway.

question: Какой максимальный тормозной путь допускается для автобуса категории M3?
notes: Braking performance is not covered. Searched 'braking distance', 'Regulation No. 13'; 'braking' only appears as a load case (heavy braking) for guards and staircases.

question: At what speed must the speed limiter be set on a long-distance coach?
notes: Searched 'speed limit', 'Regulation No. 89': none. Speeds in the text (3, 5, 20 km/h) relate to doors, steps, kneeling — not limiters.

question: Какая минимальная остаточная глубина протектора шин допускается у автобуса?
notes: Searched 'tread depth', 'tyre tread': none ('tread' only as step tread).

question: What fresh-air flow per passenger does the HVAC system have to supply?
notes: Searched 'ventilat', 'air-condition', 'air condition': only battery compartment ventilation (Annex 3 7.5.3.2). No passenger ventilation requirement.

question: Must there be a first aid kit on a trolleybus?
answer: R107 requires space for fitting one or more first-aid kits (at least 7 dm3, smallest dimension at least 80 mm); it applies to all vehicles including trolleybuses. Whether a kit must actually be carried is not set by R107.
notes: Author's original answer was 'Yes'; text requires space for the kit, not the kit itself.

question: Can the slope of the main passageway be 10% in the longitudinal direction?
answer: Depends on the class: max 8% for Classes I, II and A (so no), max 12.5% for Classes III and B (so yes).

question: Must a trolleybus be equipped with a leakage current and insulation monitoring device?
answer: Yes: an onboard device permanently monitoring leakage current or voltage between chassis and road surface, disconnecting the high-voltage circuits (when stationary) above 3 mA or 60 V DC.
